title: ICC Funded Internship -- Chambers
description: A six-month, full-time funded internship in the Chambers of the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague, Netherlands, assisting judges' legal teams with research, analysis, and drafting on international criminal law matters. Most ICC internships are unpaid, but a limited number of positions each year are funded through the ICC's Trust Fund for the Development of Interns and Visiting Professionals (supported by States Parties and other donors) specifically to improve geographic representation among interns. Funded places are reserved for nationals of a State Party to the Rome Statute that is either classified as a developing region by the UN Statistics Division, or currently the subject of an ICC investigation or preliminary examination. Funded interns receive a monthly stipend of EUR 1,125 (with a mandatory deduction for emergency health insurance) plus financial assistance toward travel costs for those not already based in the Netherlands. Visa costs are the intern's own responsibility, and interns cannot bring family members for the assignment. Candidates should hold a law degree (completed or nearing completion). Applications are open on a rolling basis with a formal deadline of 31 December 2026.
visaNote: This is an internship, not employment; visa/residence permit costs for the stay in the Netherlands are the intern's own responsibility.
